subject.title: [Bug 6.1] Silent config auto-patch from memory-core + error-message auto-fix breaks all cron jobs on hosts without Docker

question: What trust boundary should govern protected config writes that are reachable through host exec, plugin cron work, or assistant-visible error guidance?
rationale: Automation cannot safely choose whether to harden by removing model-visible config advice only, by guarding CLI config writes from agent exec, or by adding provenance/approval semantics for plugin and cron-originated mutations; that is a security and product boundary decision.

options.title: Define operator-approved config mutation boundary
options.body: Remove assistant-visible protected config assignments, add or document guardrails/provenance for non-user config writes, and keep operator CLI guidance separate from model-facing errors.

options.title: Land only error-copy hardening
options.body: Treat the linked PR shape as a partial mitigation and keep this issue open for CLI-through-exec and plugin/cron mutation provenance.

options.title: Accept current operator CLI behavior
options.body: Document that agents with host exec can run `openclaw config patch` and close only if maintainers intentionally accept that risk for trusted deployments.

recommendation.title: Define operator-approved config mutation boundary
recommendation.body: Remove assistant-visible protected config assignments, add or document guardrails/provenance for non-user config writes, and keep operator CLI guidance separate from model-facing errors.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history touches all central files, making this the best available routing owner for coordinating the cross-surface decision.
